summary.intent: Understand Callisto's competitive position against Changesets v3, Sampo, pnpm and release-please via source-level deep dives, decide how much OIDC support Callisto should own, then validate remaining audit findings against latest main and produce a handoff for Claude.
summary.outcome: Produced three research reports and a self-contained remediation handoff validated at main f5c770ca0, with four remaining findings (Python post-release precision, pre staging pathspecs, false E104 on unpublished npm cycles, broken sealed registry test fixture). Concluded Callisto should delegate OIDC to native tools. No product code changed.

repo: Changesets v3 moves consumed change files into .changeset/pre/ and changed pre.json state fields; Callisto still expects v2 fields, so its pre.json compatibility claim was overstated.
Callisto's action writes npm token config only when NPM_TOKEN is nonempty and the runner preserves OIDC env vars for npm-family tools, so npm trusted publishing is largely unobstructed.

Twine >=6.1.0 supports trusted publishing natively and Callisto pins 7.0.0, but the runner strips GitHub OIDC variables from Twine's child process, blocking it; docs/projects/OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md is stale on this.
Generated workflows are 113 lines (simple) and 376 (matrix), conflicting with the explicit <=40-line requirement due to deliberate credential-isolated publish jobs; needs an owner decision.

Production release execute requires sealed artifacts (require_sealed_publishes), so tests must run pack-npm/build-python, then artifact-manifest --seal-*, then execute with --artifact-manifest/--artifact-dir.
Sandbox native tooling needs a writable npm cache and real Rust executables rather than mise/shim paths; misconfiguration should not be classified as product defects.

pnpm reproduction: a workspace:^1.0.0 reference stayed unchanged after the dependency moved to 2.0.0, even in the packed tarball, so native consumer/packed-metadata tests matter more than bump-plan checks.

code.finding: stage_pre_json passes rel_path directly to git add, so a dir like 'notes*' glob-expands and stages neighboring notes-other/pre.json; fix with Pathspec::literal plus a -- separator (called at ~133 enter and ~189 exit).

parse_release_core strips the epoch and uses a numeric-only parser, so .post suffixes break precision detection and dependency windows widen (e.g. <1!1.3 becomes <1!2, ~=1!1.2.post1 becomes ~=1!1.2.1).

Publish-wait graph is built from the canonical identity selection before build_publish_leaves picks actual publish targets, so a cycle in unpublished npm manifests falsely yields E104 for Cargo-only publication.
Shared execute helper omits artifacts and manifest, so real-registry scenarios fail with E306 before exercising recovery; the repair must seal once and reuse the files across retries.
Callisto linked groups bump every live member, unlike Changesets which does not bump unchanged linked members, so migration can widen release scope.
Child environment policy for subprocesses determines whether OIDC variables reach Twine and npm-family tools.

workflow: Treat failing verification honestly: record unresolved failures rather than calling a run green, and separate confirmed findings from inferences.
Cloning upstream repos at pinned tags and running their CLIs on minimal fixtures gives behavioral evidence beyond reading docs.
Validate research and audit artifacts against the plugin JSON schemas with jsonschema before reporting.
Keep private audit evidence in /tmp and out of the public repo; the handoff should be self-contained and name the exact revision.

friction: entire brain brief failed on external lock-file permissions, forcing direct source inspection.
First git fetch lacked .git/FETCH_HEAD write permission and needed authorization.
Native tool setup in the sandbox (npm cache, mise shims vs real cargo) caused spurious failures that had to be separated from product defects.
The graph test suite had a Cargo registry-observation fixture failure that reproduced in isolation.
/wisp:check was unavailable in this tool surface, so the equivalent audit workflow ran manually.
An early assessment missed the stale Twine claim and the Changesets v3 prerelease state change, requiring corrections after source dives.
Generated prose from compact numeric notation needed post-hoc whitespace fix-ups in report text.
open_items: Fix the four remaining findings: QA02 Python post-release precision, QA03 pre staging pathspecs, QA05 active-output cycle projection, VR01 sealed registry fixture.
Decide whether to waive or meet the <=40-line generated-workflow requirement versus credential-isolated jobs.
Validate real tokenless npm OIDC publishing and enable Twine OIDC by letting only the uploader process receive OIDC vars; compose crates-io-auth-action for Cargo.

Refresh stale docs: OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md, REQ-DX-V1 owner-open list and registry coverage, README/publishing/config packing wording, ROAD-TO-V1 cargo-semver-checks proposal, stderr JSON contract wording.
Reconcile Changesets v3 pre.json compatibility and migration differences (linked, peer bumps, ignored config keys).
Run full just ci/90% coverage, just verify-real after fixture repair, hosted OIDC, onboarding timing and platform install/load matrix, none of which were run.
Investigate two unconfirmed fallback-only canonical-vs-active projection probes.
Consider head-to-head failure-recovery rehearsals against Sampo/Changesets and a five-owner alpha experiment.
